evidence: The atmosphere within the second floor is characterized by its solemnity and reverence, with high-ceilinged rooms adorned with brightly painted walls and softly illuminated by yellow lights. Dominant throughout are the rich tones of wood, complemented by the stark contrasts of black-and-white archival photographs and the faded hues of aged paper and fabric.

The atmosphere within the second floor is characterized by its solemnity and reverence, with high-ceilinged rooms adorned with brightly painted walls and softly illuminated by yellow lights. Dominant throughout are the rich tones of wood, complemented by the stark contrasts of black-and-white archival photographs and the faded hues of aged paper and fabric.

Large photographs of the revolutionary movement line the walls, serving as poignant reminders of the era’s defining moments. These images are surrounded by glass display cases housing various artifacts, including old leaflets, photographs, and simple objects once used by soldiers, all of which contribute to a deeply immersive experience for visitors.
